{"task": {"id": "I_kwDOVQjdzc8AAAABio6Wqw", "item_id": "PVTI_lAHOAHSLSM4Bn3IVzhL_dmY", "project_id": "PVT_kwHOAHSLSM4Bn3IV", "number": 257, "title": "Redesign the Saturn player UI and add responsive full touch controls", "body": "## Problem

The browser demo should feel like a game player rather than a boot-configuration/debugging tool. The current Saturn page has a permanent three-step setup panel, separate Start and Pause/Resume controls, extensive inline explanatory text, a large fullscreen control allowance, and no volume slider or touchscreen controller.

The requester wants the UI/UX and responsive layout improved by using the same author's SNES and WonderSwan demos as references, **including mobile touch controls in the same implementation and Issue**. Do not split the desktop redesign and mobile controller into separate tasks or close this Issue with only one of them implemented.

## Expected outcome

Deliver a coherent, minimal, responsive **saturn-rust** player with a prominent game screen, compact playback controls, a disc/BIOS slot area, contextual Help/Advanced controls, volume adjustment, and a complete touch controller on suitable mobile/touch layouts. Preserve the existing emulator, media-selection behavior, CRT effects and debugger functionality.

Follow the repository's [UI/UX principles](../blob/main/README.md#uiux): keep it simple, show rather than tell, and make controls intuitive and predictable. Preserve accessible names, necessary warnings, recovery actions, user decisions and destructive-action safeguards.

### Layout and visual hierarchy

- Use the same general visual language as the sibling demos: a restrained light page with a dark game-screen surround, compact `saturn-rust` branding, Help and GitHub links, consistent spacing, typography and control styling. Do not add a promotional landing page or bundled game catalogue.
- Make the display the largest and most prominent element. On desktop, place compact Disc and BIOS summaries/actions beside the screen when space permits; do not retain the large numbered boot wizard. On narrow screens put the screen and its controls before the media configuration, with media selection reachable without hunting through long help text.
- Group the everyday controls into one compact toolbar: Play/Pause/Resume, Reset (existing restart behavior), mute and volume, Display filter, Fullscreen. A single primary playback action reflects the current state rather than presenting competing Start and Resume actions. Retain loading, readiness and error status where it is useful; move verbose technical explanations to Help/Advanced.
- Keep the screen's existing resolution/aspect policy and pixel/CRT presentation. Make fullscreen use the available viewport for the actual image, rather than reserving the current fixed 240px allowance. Retain an accessible exit control; keep touch controls reachable in touch fullscreen. Respect safe-area insets, orientation and viewport resizing.

### Disc and BIOS

- Replace the permanent file-input wizard with clearly labeled current Disc and BIOS entries and compact Insert/Change/Clear actions. Use a small accessible dialog/popover or a similarly direct file picker; keep drag-and-drop and multi-file CUE + BINARY selection. Show the selected disc/BIOS name and pending/invalid/error state without requiring users to inspect a debugger. Long filenames must not break layout.
- Preserve CHD v5, ISO, CUE/BIN and the existing explicitly referenced diagnostic companion format and bounds. Do not add a disc/ROM library, automatic media downloads, IndexedDB media retention, or new media formats.
- Preserve automatic boot selection from #135: a valid selected 512 KiB BIOS takes precedence (disc optional); disc-only uses HLE; neither disables Play. Pending/invalid/failed BIOS selection must block launch, never silently fall back to HLE. Clear/reselect explicitly to recover. Changing media stops playback, rejects stale asynchronous results and retains independently valid selections. Restart retains accepted media and backup RAM.
- Keep genuine firmware and disc bytes local to the current tab; do not copy the siblings' ROM-storage policy. No automatic persistence of disc, BIOS or backup data.

### Audio, help and diagnostics

- Add a keyboard/touch-accessible mute control and volume slider (0–100%, with current value available). A muted state preserves the selected volume; changing volume or muting must not alter guest PCM, speed, timing or reset state. Use the existing audio pipeline, with output gain or equivalent bounded host-side volume control. Start audio on the normal Play gesture where the browser permits; if blocked, show the existing actionable Enable audio recovery rather than losing audio silently. Preserve pause, underrun reporting and existing slow-playback/pitch behavior.
- Move keyboard/gamepad instructions, media formats, privacy and compatibility notes into compact Help. Keep Advanced/Debug reachable for all current CPU/frame/fixture controls, register displays, backup RAM import/export and diagnostics. Do not delete functionality or expose technical setup by default. A dialog must have a labeled close action, sensible focus management and Escape behavior. Preserve existing pause/release semantics and never auto-resume a previously paused session merely because a dialog closes or the tab becomes visible.
- Retain the existing four display modes from #254: Clean (default), CRT Composite, CRT S-Video and CRT RGB, with context-loss/unsupported-GPU fallback and live/paused redraw. Do not expand or rewrite shaders for the layout change.

### Mobile and touch controller (required in this Issue)

- Add a virtual Player 1 standard Saturn digital controller: four D-pad directions, diagonals, A/B/C, X/Y/Z, L/R, Start. Lay out the six face buttons as two recognizable rows (X/Y/Z above A/B/C). Preserve the physical button identities and existing keyboard/gamepad mappings; do not change the meaning of buttons on rotation.
- On portrait touch layouts, place the screen above a compact controller. On landscape touch layouts, place directional/shoulder and face/shoulder controls on either side of the screen when feasible, with a usable Start button. Choose a responsive fallback arrangement for constrained dimensions instead of clipping or overlapping the display or shrinking buttons to unusable sizes. Prefer 44 CSS px touch targets and maintain them in the supported layouts. Do not permanently show the virtual controller on normal fine-pointer desktop layouts.
- Use pointer events with per-pointer ownership and capture (or an equivalent robust implementation). Support D-pad sliding/diagonals, simultaneous presses by multiple fingers, independent release of each pointer/button, and cancellation. Merge touch masks with keyboard and gamepad masks without one source releasing a button still held by another source. Route the input through the existing emulated controller/SMPC path, including the existing 3D-pad digital overlay semantics where applicable.
- Release held input on pointer cancellation/lost capture, blur, tab hiding, pause, reset/restart, media replacement, Help/Advanced/Debug and fullscreen transitions as appropriate. Do not leave stuck buttons, hijack unrelated page gestures, or unexpectedly resume playback. Preserve ordinary page scrolling outside the controller.
- Support touch fullscreen with safe-area-aware layout, all controls reachable and no unintended overlay obscuring the image. No requirement for second-player touch controls, analog virtual sticks or additional peripherals.

## Context and reproduction

Baseline: `main` at `194eb5c9b81db979e27e57514d34f7f9a0579911`. The existing CRT implementation (#254) is already merged. This is a UX enhancement rather than a single reproducible crash.

Reference the actual sibling frontend sources rather than copying their product-specific state/storage policies:

- [snes-rust player HTML](https://github.com/takahirox/snes-rust/blob/main/web/index.html), [CSS](https://github.com/takahirox/snes-rust/blob/main/web/style.css), [demo](https://takahirox.github.io/snes-rust/): compact cartridge popover, Help header, volume and display controls, portrait/landscape touch layouts and display-centered fullscreen.
- [wonderswan-rust player HTML](https://github.com/takahirox/wonderswan-rust/blob/main/web/index.html), [CSS](https://github.com/takahirox/wonderswan-rust/blob/main/web/src/style.css), [demo](https://takahirox.github.io/wonderswan-rust/): compact media panel, Help dialog, optional diagnostics, safe-area-aware touch/fullscreen layouts and display selection.
- Saturn: `web/index.html`, `web/style.css`, `web/app.js`, `web/audio.js`, `web/audio-worklet.js`, `web/crt-display.js`, Worker presentation/input interfaces and existing browser tests. Existing Saturn desktop grid reserves 310–380px for setup; at <=900px it puts the setup before the screen. Current fullscreen subtracts 240px from viewport height. Replace these constraints with responsive content-driven layout. Relevant completed Issues: #134 (buttons), #135 (auto boot), #254 (CRT). Do not alter their behavioral contracts.

Keep the work focused on this complete frontend improvement. No unrelated framework migration, emulator core/timing changes, per-game fixes or requirement to solve #17/#138.

## Pre-merge acceptance criteria

**All mandatory criteria below must be executable and verifiable by the implementation agent using automated tests and source/measurement evidence. No human sign-off, manual visual approval, physical phone/tablet/controller, proprietary BIOS/game, or deployed-site verification is required for implementation, merge or Issue closure.** Follow [development flow](https://github.com/takahirox/saturn-rust/blob/main/docs/development-flow.md), [review guidelines](https://github.com/takahirox/saturn-rust/blob/main/docs/review-guidelines.md) and [CI principles](https://github.com/takahirox/saturn-rust/blob/main/docs/ci-performance.md). Existing repository review/protection requirements remain unchanged.

- [ ] **Unified player UI:** remove the numbered boot wizard; show one main display, compact playback toolbar, Disc/BIOS summaries and accessible selection actions, Help and hidden-by-default diagnostics. Verify DOM/accessible names, action states, focus and keyboard operation in production browser tests. No duplicate primary playback actions or always-visible lengthy instructions.
- [ ] **Responsive layout:** automated Chromium viewport/device-emulation tests for desktop (e.g. 1280×720 and 1440×900), phone portrait (320×568 and 390×844), phone landscape (844×390), and a tablet-sized viewport. Test fine/coarse pointer modes, DPR and orientation changes. Use computed bounds, scroll widths, visibility, hit testing and aspect-ratio checks to prove screen-first mobile ordering, no horizontal page overflow or clipped/overlapping essential controls, and usable touch targets; check fullscreen image fits its available space with working exit and touch controls. Save representative original-guest screenshots as optional agent-readable evidence, not a subjective approval gate. Test normal and unusually long media labels and actual error messages.
- [ ] **Media and session flow:** original licensed BIOS/disc guests exercise every auto-mode combination, invalid/pending BIOS, explicit clearing/replacement, delayed overlapping reads, CHD/ISO/multi-file CUE, disc drag/drop, Play/Pause/Reset, backup preservation and recovery. No unexpected restart/resume, silent HLE fallback, network transfer or persistent media storage. Existing media and boot behavior remains intact.
- [ ] **Volume and audio:** production browser tests prove monotonic output gain at representative slider settings including 0 and 100, mute/unmute restoration, nonzero guest sound, Play-gesture audio activation and blocked-audio recovery, while preserving original source PCM and audio pipeline behavior. Verify bounded queues, pause and reset semantics; do not require real audio hardware or listening by a person.
- [ ] **Complete touch input:** use Playwright/CDP emulated touch or equivalent automated pointer tests with original guest-visible controller reports. Verify each of the thirteen digital controls, diagonal D-pad, simultaneous independent pointers, face/shoulder/direction combinations, slide, cancellation and release; test touch plus keyboard/gamepad union and focus/modal/pause/reset/media/fullscreen/orientation transitions. Assert actual SMPC/guest results, not merely CSS pressed states. Verify desktop keyboard and both physical-gamepad mappings through synthetic Standard Gamepad states without real hardware.
- [ ] **Display and Advanced:** preserve clean pixels, all CRT modes/fallback and paused redraw, dynamic aspect/resolution, fullscreen and raw framebuffer checks. Prove existing Help/Advanced/Debug, CPU stepping, original bootstrap fixture, backup RAM import/export and input-release behavior remain accessible and correct. Dialog focus return and Escape do not accidentally advance guest time or resume playback.
- [ ] **Performance and accessibility:** preserve Worker credits, frame delivery, audio and timing contracts. Avoid polling/layout work per frame that is not needed; use the existing optimized render path. Run a bounded repeatable original-guest comparison of previous/current Clean normal playback (fixed work, throughput/presentation gaps and audio queue drops), report measured variation and investigate meaningful regressions. Do not make a hardware-specific 60 FPS threshold an acceptance gate. Verify focus indicators, labels, disabled states, status announcements and controller targets through automated checks.
- [ ] **Documentation and validation:** update README/setup/control help and a focused validation record with objective test results, tested viewports, input mappings and known limits. Run applicable formatting, locked native build/tests/Clippy, fixture checks, production compatible/accelerated Wasm build and browser/CI runner tests per the repository's current tooling; require successful applicable exact-head PR CI before merge. Extend existing test groups where possible rather than duplicating expensive suites. Do not weaken guest timing/pixel/PCM/input assertions or artifact/publication checks. Close this single Issue after successful merge once all required desktop and mobile criteria are satisfied.

## Optional validation

None needed for closure. Physical devices, real controllers, subjective appearance feedback and authorized personal BIOS/game trials may be useful later, but are not requested deliverables or blockers. Automated original-guest and emulated-device checks are the acceptance evidence.

## Required post-merge verification

None. Do not keep this Issue open awaiting a person, a live Pages deployment check or subjective design acceptance.
